# What would give C's order on a listing

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`what-would-give-c` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F07 · [record](what-would-give-c.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> Beside what reads no order and holds, a premise giving C implies it. On a listing, widening is what no chooser, over every valuation, does worse from and some better from; where every item is someone's own, what every self-concerned profile not ranking it below ranks by Pareto. Each reads an order.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. Call a premise on orders strictly weaker than C at a datum where C implies it and some order meets it and fails C. Let help read no order and hold at a datum. A premise that gives C there with that help implies C there, so no order meets it and fails C, and such a premise that C also implies is C there. So no premise is both strictly weaker than C at a datum and, with such help holding there, enough for C there. It can, where it reads the datum, give C at one datum and be strictly weaker at another; it can be weaker in scope; or it can fail to give C with that help. (`Becoming.ReadsNoOrder.implies_comparison`, `Becoming.ReadsNoOrder.not_strictly_weaker`, `Becoming.ReadsNoOrder.iff_of_weaker`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* no shared law's anchor among the constants its declarations use.
2. On a frame reading a course by what it admits on a listing, with the process free and every claim counted as living, so that scope is already total, an extension is a widening and an order meets C exactly when it is increasing in admission. There, with every listed item marked, an order is self-concerned exactly when it meets C, through the law above: one premise in two forms. (`Becoming.Weighting.listingFrame`, `Becoming.Weighting.extension_listingFrame_iff`, `Becoming.Weighting.comparison_listingFrame_iff`, `Becoming.Weighting.increasingInOwn_iff_comparison`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* widening; its declarations do not reach the grammar.
3. A chooser is a pair of values, none asserted to exist: a valuation of the listed items and a value of refusing, both fixed across courses; it takes one item, so it reaches the highest of refusal and what a course admits. A course including another is never lower for it, near-definitionally; added items it would each leave change nothing. One course widens another exactly when no chooser does worse by its own valuation and some does better by its own, a merely possible chooser counting, and an order is increasing in admission exactly when it ranks above whatever that holds of. On a mixed pair each course is better for some chooser. (`Becoming.Weighting.reach`, `Becoming.Weighting.reach_le_of_includes`, `Becoming.Weighting.reach_eq_of_refused`, `Becoming.Weighting.outside`, `Becoming.Weighting.NoneWorseSomeBetter`, `Becoming.Weighting.widens_iff_noneWorseSomeBetter`, `Becoming.Weighting.increasing_iff_ranks_noneWorseSomeBetter`, `Becoming.Weighting.choosers_mixed`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* widening; its declarations do not reach the grammar.
4. What a range of choosers has to hold is exact: for every widening some chooser in it does better, exactly when, for each listed item, some chooser in it puts that item above every other listed item and above refusal. (`Becoming.Weighting.gains_every_widening_iff`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* widening; its declarations do not reach the grammar.
5. The route stops at witnesses. Imposed, an item a net weighting counts below zero can put a widening below what it widens, while a chooser who leaves it is unchanged. Where the chooser's order is not the order reading the result, the chooser can gain and what it takes stand lower in that order. Where a choice bears on what the other gets, widening the one menu both choose from can lower what each gets by the game's payoffs at the only mutual best response, the pure Nash equilibrium of one play; where no choice bears, it cannot. (`Becoming.Weighting.Refusing.widens`, `Becoming.Weighting.Refusing.imposed_below`, `Becoming.Weighting.Refusing.refused_unchanged`, `Becoming.Weighting.AnotherReads.widens`, `Becoming.Weighting.AnotherReads.takes_narrow`, `Becoming.Weighting.AnotherReads.takes_wide`, `Becoming.Weighting.AnotherReads.chooser_gains`, `Becoming.Weighting.AnotherReads.reading_falls`, `Becoming.Weighting.MutualBest`, `Becoming.Weighting.Restraint.widens`, `Becoming.Weighting.Restraint.narrow_best`, `Becoming.Weighting.Restraint.wide_best_iff`, `Becoming.Weighting.Restraint.each_falls`, `Becoming.Weighting.not_lowered_of_no_bearing`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* widening; its declarations do not reach the grammar.
6. All three relate their courses by the same widening, so on the frame above, every claim counted, every order meeting C ranks the wider above the narrower while the net weighting falls, what the chooser takes stands lower in the reading order, or what each gets falls. Whether a menu of acts is a course of what can form is not shown. The last witness is a theorem on that frame; its bearing on courses of what can form, and so on C, stands until the full account is shown to remove it, by showing that no wider course has its shape: one course widening another while, at the pure Nash equilibrium of one play among those choosing within it, what each gets falls. If one has it, it stands against C there too. (`Becoming.Weighting.Refusing.comparison_ranks_wide`, `Becoming.Weighting.AnotherReads.comparison_ranks_wide`, `Becoming.Weighting.Restraint.comparison_ranks_wide`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* widening; its declarations do not reach the grammar.
7. Over profiles in which each standpoint's order is increasing in its own continuation and ranks no widening below what it widens, one course is ranked above another by every profile's Pareto relation exactly when it widens the other and adds to some standpoint's own; so every such relation is increasing in admission exactly when every listed item is someone's own, and a standpoint whose marking leaves a listed item need not have an order that is. 8. An order ranking below every widening that adds nothing to its own is self-concerned, and the Pareto relation then does not rank such a widening, whatever the others' orders. On three listed items no positive weighting's order is exactly widening: it would tie two mixed pairs and weigh the third item nothing. 9. Given a widening by one item, a transitive order is increasing in admission exactly when every such widening gets one verdict and the given one is ranked. An order ranking the course of lower total weight above, on positive weights, meets all of it but the given comparison; an order counting one item and not another, one ranking only something above nothing, one ranking only widenings by more than one item, and one not transitive each show a part doing its own work. 10. Where everything downstream of a center is alike to it under a class and a marking holds what its line reaches, on a listing of what lies downstream an order increasing in its own continuation is increasing in admission. Constancy of the class up to the net's end at the center, with the class holding its effects, gives that the class holds it, and so the same law. <a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- No axiom. A finite listing of items; two-valued admission; natural-number values and weights; one refusal value for all items; an order a relation on courses. Equality of items decided for the range's law, the Pareto relation's covering law and the one-item law.
- Choosers: what is left costing nothing, which the maximum builds in; a chooser who takes one item; its values, its refusal and its being there at all fixed across courses; "later" a reading, with no time in what it reaches and no chooser asserted to exist; each choosing alone, by its own order; the range over every valuation and every value of refusing, or the range stated in the range's law.
- Standpoints: each order increasing in its own continuation and ranking no widening below; the Pareto relation counting a silent standpoint as no objection. A pure Nash equilibrium read as a mutual best response from one menu, in one play with no binding agreement, not as what actual choosers do. The listing's frame reads a course by what it admits, every claim counted, the process free.
- What lies downstream: a class on the root; everything downstream of the center alike to it, or constancy up to the net's end at its class with the class holding its effects; a marking holding what its line reaches; a listing of what lies downstream.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- A reason for C: calling better what no chooser does worse from and some does better from, self-concern at each standpoint, and one verdict on every one-item widening are each a premise reading an order.
- That C derives from the continuation condition: nothing here does. What reads no order and holds gives C only if every order meets C (the first law, at a premise every order meets), which an extension rules out.
- That no valuing enters at all: some chooser doing better comes from the range, and a chooser who would leave everything added gains nothing. Witness: `Becoming.Weighting.reach_eq_of_refused`.
- That more options are better: among several choosers a wider menu can lower what each gets at the pure Nash equilibrium of one play. Whether a wider course of what can form can do the same is open; if one can, the witness stands against C there too, with the shape T8's refuter had until 9 November 2026. Witness: `Becoming.Weighting.Restraint.each_falls`.
- What is no one's own: not every such profile ranks a widening adding only that. With standpoints read as present ones a future beyond every present line is such an item, and so read the route does not do the step of invariance's work; which formations hold standpoints is open.
- C on a frame of what can form, past the listing's frame: the routes end in an order on a listing, which gives C between level paths only with admission decided and both paths' admissions listed, one way, and no route here gives C on all of a web's level paths.
- A chooser who learns across a deferred irreversible step: values are fixed and there is no time in what it reaches, so quasi-option value is not captured; nor refusal at a price.
- That a premise weaker at other data is any easier to argue for: not a question the Lean can answer.
- **Counterexample:** Against reading C as more options are better, and as what C does on the listing's frame: on two listed acts the wider menu widens the narrower, every order meeting C on that frame ranks it above, and at the only mutual best response of each what each gets falls from 2 to 1 (Weighting.Restraint.widens, Weighting.Restraint.comparison_ranks_wide, Weighting.Restraint.narrow_best, Weighting.Restraint.wide_best_iff, Weighting.Restraint.each_falls). On that frame it is a theorem; its bearing on courses of what can form stands until the full account is shown to remove it. [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/RoutesToC.lean)
- **Counterexample:** Against the chooser route where admission is imposed: one item a net weighting counts below zero puts the widening below what it widens, while every order meeting C on the listing's frame ranks it above (Weighting.Refusing.imposed_below, Weighting.Refusing.comparison_ranks_wide). Nothing in a course's admitting a formation makes the formation chosen. [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/RoutesToC.lean)
- **Counterexample:** Against the chooser route where another's order reads the result: the wider course lets the chooser do better by its order and what it takes stands lower in the other, while every order meeting C on the listing's frame ranks it above (Weighting.AnotherReads.chooser_gains, Weighting.AnotherReads.reading_falls, Weighting.AnotherReads.comparison_ranks_wide). [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/RoutesToC.lean)
- **Counterexample:** Against one verdict on every one-item widening, with transitivity, giving an order increasing in admission: the order ranking the course of lower total weight above has both and reverses every widening (Weighting.ranksLighter_transitive, Weighting.ranksLighter_alike, Weighting.ranksLighter_reverses). [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/RoutesToC.lean)

<a id="correspondence--对应"></a>
### Correspondence

Choosers: Foster's effective freedom (1993; 2011) with every preference admitted, set inclusion, on a list, with refusal an item in every menu; what a chooser reaches is one state's term in Kreps's (1979) representation of a preference for flexibility, which aggregates what this intersects; the range's law is Nehring and Puppe's (1999) condition for an element to add strictly, at every listed item. Another's order: the shape of Strotz's inconsistency (1955-56), a discount shifting with the date rather than tastes changing unexpectedly, and of temptation without self-control (Gul and Pesendorfer 2001); the witness has no time and does not say the two orders are one person's. Several choosers: the prisoner's dilemma read as a menu, the shape also of Braess's paradox (1968), and against the thesis G. Dworkin (1982) examines; that a chooser can gain by having fewer options is older than Schelling: Strotz has it against one's later self, by precluding future options; Schelling (1960) has it toward another, by binding oneself in a threat or a promise. Standpoints: the Pareto relation over self-concerned orders. One item at a time: an order's verdict made uniform; that an order need not tell small steps apart is the idea of Luce's semiorders (1956); the order here is one on at most three listed items and not from four (by enumeration, not in Lean), a mixed pair staying unranked however large its difference. Reading (the AI's): beside help that reads no order, "weaker" has other data or scope open; the range of valuations does the work positivity does.
